conclusions.search_post_note: name_field_used was null — script field-name matching did not resolve txtNameKeywords1. POST sent empty payload and server returned the blank search form unchanged (identical 13,186 bytes). Form field names are confirmed: txtNameKeywords1, txtNameKeywords2, txtCompanyNumber. A corrected POST targeting txtNameKeywords1 directly would execute the search. This is a script gap, not a CADO access block.
conclusions.value_added_exact_quote: the CADO user shall not copy, distribute, loan, lease, sell or use data as part of a value added product or otherwise make the data available to any other party without the prior written approval of Government of Newfoundland and Labrador
conclusions.commercial_automation_permitted: PROHIBITED — disclaimer explicitly prohibits use as part of a value added product, distribution to another party, copying, leasing, or selling without prior written Government approval
conclusions.classification_reason: The CADO disclaimer contains an explicit prohibition on using registry data as part of a value-added product or making it available to another party without prior written NL Government approval. This pipeline is a commercial B2B prospecting product — that use is directly and unambiguously covered by the restriction. Technical accessibility (search page loads, no auth required, fields confirmed) is irrelevant; the licensing gate is closed without a written agreement.
conclusions.architectural_note: CADO could serve as a manual targeted-verification tool for individual NL company lookups (identity confirmation, status, registration number) where those lookups are not feeding a value-added data product. That narrow use would still require legal review of the prior-written-approval clause. For the automated pipeline, NL has no confirmed free/open alternative at this time.
